content.overview: Specialist instruction for donor suitability, health & performance history in donor/mother plant systems.

sections.title: Suitability uses multiple evidence streams
sections.body: Donor condition, developmental status, cutting quality, recent stress, propagation success, plant-health history and identity confidence all affect whether a donor should supply material.

sections.title: Asymptomatic does not mean pathogen-free
sections.body: HLVd has been detected in asymptomatic stock plants and rooted vegetative cuttings, so visual health alone cannot establish clean-stock status.

sections.title: Performance trends can reveal source-linked problems
sections.body: When one donor repeatedly underperforms under comparable process conditions, preserve that signal and investigate source, condition, genotype, handling and plant-health evidence before changing a shared room process.

commonMistakes: Treating visual health as proof of clean-stock status.
content.practicalApplication: Review a donor-management scenario, preserve identity and status evidence, and document the strongest supported next action without overstating cause or cleanliness.
content.summary: Donor management depends on traceable identity, plant-health evidence, controlled movement and longitudinal performance records.
